item.title: Ambrym (Vanuatu) - Report for 16 September-22 September 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Vanuatu Meteorology and Geo-Hazards Department (VMGD) reported that a new eruption at Ambrym likely started on 19 September. An intense thermal anomaly and high sulfur dioxide emissions were identified in satellite data; a volcanic cloud was visible in a satellite image at 0600. Ground-based observers reported dark gray ash-and-gas plumes rising from Marum Crater and rumbling sounds coming from the crater. Minor ashfall was reported in areas downwind, including in communities to the W, NW…

item.title: Chikurachki (Russia) - Report for 16 September-22 September 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT) reported that an explosive eruption at Chikurachki likely began at 1830 on 20 September based on satellite data and advisories issued by the Tokyo Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC). Ash plumes rose as high as 3 km (10,000 ft) a.s.l. and drifted 140 km NE and E. Explosions continued intermittently through the next day. item.title: Tokachidake (Japan) - Report for 16 September-22 September 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description: The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported that volcanic activity at Tokachidake continued to intensify. Inflation at relatively shallow depths began to be detected in March.
